text:
incident-bot: Pager: GPU queue length for pool 'infer-prod-a' > 95% for 12m, pending queue growth, autoscaler attempted scale but max reached. TAG: severity=page, impact=partial.
Maya (oncall): seeing high tail latency, UI shows lots of queued requests, customers likely hitting 5-10s extra latency. investigating.
Javier (sre): logs show repeated driver resets and Xid 31/13 in kernel logs on 3 nodes. possible driver/runtime instability causing effective capacity loss.
Alice Chen (runtime): copying log snippet: ```kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, pid=4321 fault: GPU exception```. Also runtime shows many models force-evicted due to OOM while serving longer sequences.
Tomas (infra-oncall): autoscaler status: tried to increase node count from 120 -> 160 but cloud quota prevented further provisioning. cloud quota error: "Exceeded quota: GPUs per region". So autoscaler is hitting a hard cap.
Maya (oncall): so two issues: (1) runtime/driver instability reducing available GPUs, (2) autoscaler can't add more because of quota. Combined effect = queue growth.
Samir (eng-lead): priority = page. Need immediate mitigations to stop customer-facing failures. Suggestions?
Alice Chen (runtime): quick mitigations we can do right now: - reduce concurrency per instance to limit KV cache blowups - disable long-sequence models on hot routes (switch to shorter-context model variant) - enable prefix KV caching more aggressively for repeated prompts.
Javier (sre): infra mitigations: cordon+drain nodes showing Xid errors, roll nodes through a driver version pinned to 525.85 (known stable for these jobs). But draining will temporarily reduce capacity further.
Tomas (infra-oncall): I can start cordoning two worst nodes and trigger a rolling reboot with forced driver re-install. Need greenlight.
Maya (oncall): do it but we need to avoid cascading evictions. Plan: 1) set autoscaler max temporarily to +50 above current (if cloud quota change possible) 2) cordon/drain 2 nodes at a time 3) reduce model concurrency on router to avoid immediate backpressure.
Priya (cust-suc): flagging customers: two enterprise tenants seeing 20-30% higher latency and some 5xxs. I have a support DM thread open with both. Will send incident comms once we have mitigation ETA.
deploy-bot: Deploy request queued: revert to runtime image v3.8.1-hotfix? -- blocked by autoscaler capacity.
Javier (sre): immediate workaround if quota cannot be bumped: spin up CPU-backed fallback workers for non-latency-sensitive embeddings/low-priority jobs and throttle heavy gen routes to preserve tokens for PLG traffic. Might limit degradation for paying customers.
Maya (oncall): action items I'm executing now: - throttle low-priority route /api/v1/gen-heavy (routing weight -> 0.2) - patch router to route to smaller model variants for two noisy customers - cordon node gpu-12 and gpu-19 and start driver reinstall.
Alice Chen (runtime): note: kernel OOM sometimes triggered by large KV caches for multi-turn sessions. We'll reduce session retention window to 30s for hot models.
Tomas (infra-oncall): cordoned gpu-12,gpu-19. draining... pod evictions in progress (approx 12 pods each).
Maya (oncall): update: queue growth slowed from 1200 -> 420 pending after throttles and smaller model routing. Latency for priority customers back to +3s rather than +8-12s.
Priya (cust-suc): communicated to affected customers with ETA ~45m for full mitigation. one customer wants SLA credit estimation, collecting details.
Javier (sre): observed on gpu-19 after reboot: driver crash count dropped to zero for 10m. kernel logs show fewer Xid entries. Good sign.
Samir (eng-lead): can we avoid full fleet reboot? what's root cause hypotheses?
Alice Chen (runtime): probable hypotheses: - recent driver kernel module mismatch from last node image update + certain attention kernels cause GPU memory corruption -> Xid - bad memory patterns from a particular model variant under long sequences - overheating? but no thermals reported.
Maya (oncall): we still have 7 nodes with intermittent Xid spikes. Tomas, can we mark them for next-wave rolling reboot and hold until autoscaler gets room?
Tomas (infra-oncall): I can queue next-wave but cloud quota still stuck. I opened ticket with cloud support to request a temporary GPU quota bump for region us-west-2. reference #CS-8221.
deploy-bot: note: revert runtime image to v3.8.1-hotfix initiated by Alice Chen. Will start staged deploy to 10% canary after nodes are cordoned to reduce risk.
Maya (oncall): monitoring: error-rate graph shows 502 spikes down to 2% for paid routes, earlier hit 7%. Good progress. Keep throttles for 30m more.
Priya (cust-suc): customers notified. one enterprise asks for postmortem and timeline; I'll coordinate with eng.
Javier (sre): temporary mitigation summary: throttles + smaller model routing + cordon/reboot two nodes at a time + KV retention window lowered. Next: autoscaler quota bump or manual soft-lift of autoscaler by infra.
Samir (eng-lead): next steps for root cause: collect driver panics + coredumps from nodes, reproduce on staging with same driver+runtime config and long sequences. assign to Alice + Javier.
Maya (oncall): handoff: Tomas will take overnight watch; I'll be offline in 15m. Tomas, please track cloud support response and node reboots, keep throttles until green.
Tomas (infra-oncall): acknowledged. I'll post updates in this thread. Filed cloud support request, ETA 2h. Starting rolling reboots on the 7 flagged nodes in waves of 2.
Priya (cust-suc): I have outgoing customer message drafted, will send after Tomas confirms next-wave targets.
Javier (sre): tagging: @Samir will own postmortem and severity classification. We should capture timeline, root cause, mitigations, and SLA impact.
Maya (oncall): handing off oncall to Tomas. Pager clear for me.
Tomas (infra-oncall): handoff ack. Current status: pending queue = 320, autoscaler at max due to quota, cloud ticket open #CS-8221, next reboot wave in 8m.
incident-bot: Incident status changed: active -> mitigated (partial). Follow-up actions: postmortem, driver-pin release, autoscaler policy review.
Samir (eng-lead): thanks team. Please add logs and snippets to the postmortem doc and tag cust-suc responses. We will schedule an infra/runtime sync tomorrow to finalize fixes.
Priya (cust-suc): will attach customer impact notes.
Maya (oncall): final note before signoff: if you see Xid > 3 on any node, remove it from pool immediately and tag for driver rollback.
Tomas (infra-oncall): understood. I'll continue rolling reboots and escalate cloud quota if no response in 2h.
Maya (oncall): signing off. Thanks all :thumbsup:
